name: Reddish wine
lede: Reddish wine glosses Azuki-iro, a Japanese traditional name taken from the dark red azuki bean.

sections.title: Named for a bean
sections.body:
The library files this hex under *Azuki-iro* (小豆色), named for the azuki bean, a small dark-red legume used across East Asian cooking [1]. The English gloss "Reddish wine" describes the hue's deep brownish-red rather than translating the bean's name [1]. The hex #672422 is a screen approximation; no exact date for this named shade is recorded in the sources consulted here [1].

Its nearest library look-alike is [[light-oxblood]], about 2.7 units away in LCH space [1].

Further along the same family are [[persian-plum]], more vivid, and [[chestnut-leather-brown]], almost the same color [1]. [[oxblood]] names the wider family this shade belongs to [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue appears in 757 of 23,781 paintings, about 3.2 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks around the 1470s, with Andrea del Sarto and Giorgione among the painters who use it most relative to their output, and it is common again in the 1400s and 1500s more broadly [2]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
